title: Structured output heuristics playbook — fn/tool parse triage
content:
Context:
- Quick personal playbook for triaging structured-output / function-call parsing failures encountered while validating model responses (local dev and hosted).
- Goal: fast reproducible triage, isolate whether problem is model, prompt, post-processor, or SDK/transport layer.

Recent incident summary (short):
- Date: 2024-10-29 08:42 PDT — intermittent JSON parse failures in prod route: /v1/generate/chat -> tool_invoke handler. ~0.3% of requests in a 2h window.
- Symptoms: client receives HTTP 200 with body streaming, final chunk contains malformed JSON (extra trailing comma OR duplicated key). SDK JSON.parse throws. Downstream tool integration fails silently.
- First-pass: rate spike correlated with a rollout of prompt tweak (pr#842). But repro is flaky locally.

Repro steps / minimal checks (run in order):
1) Capture raw streaming transcript (prefer server trace with token-level recording).
   - curl to hosted API with ?log=verbose or use internal trace endpoint.
2) Re-run the same request synchronously using the exact model & params pinned in logs (model id + seed if available).
3) If streaming, try non-streaming to force full response buffer — sometimes streaming chunking logic is the culprit.
4) Run the post-processor (JS JSON.parse) against the exact bytes recorded by server. Paste into a local file response.raw.json and run `node -e \"console.log(JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('response.raw.json','utf8')))\`` to reproduce.

Observed error snippets (copied from logs):
- "Unexpected token } in JSON at position 1423"
- Partial output sample (sanitized):
  {
    \"action\": \"update_db\",
    \"args\": {
      \"user_id\": 12345,
      \"changes\": [
        {
          \"field\": \"email\",
          \"value\": \"x@example.com\"
        },
      ],
    },
  }
- Notes: trailing commas after arrays/objects observed above. Also saw duplicated "args" keys once.

Commands tried so far (local):
- curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -d @payload.json https://api-redwood/staging/v1/chat/generate > resp.raw && jq . resp.raw  # fails with parse error
- python3 -c \"import json,sys;print(json.loads(open('resp.raw').read()))\"  # raises JSONDecodeError with pos
- node streaming test to simulate chunk boundaries (split response at bytes N and resume) — when split boundary falls inside an escape sequence, parser fails

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Model occasionally emits trailing commas or stray punctuation when asked to produce JSON (prompt drift). Likely when asked to include comments or explainers in same output.
2) Streaming reassembly bug: chunk boundary handling in SDK or gateway inserts an extra comma when stitching 'emit' frames (edge case in array concatenation logic).
3) Post-processing unwrap code mistakenly concatenates partial JSON fragments (e.g., header + body) without checking for separator — introduced in recent SDK change.
4) Data encoding issue: non-UTF8 byte sequences cause parser to drop chars, producing structural errors.

Quick heuristics to check each hypothesis:
- H1 (model): run deterministic, non-streaming call with same prompt and high temperature 0.0. If error persists, model likely at fault. Also inspect tokens around errors via token-level sampling.
- H2 (streaming): reproduce with small manual chunk sizes and verify reassembled bytes vs original. Use `xxd` or `hexdump` to compare.
- H3 (post-processor): bypass SDK entirely — call API via curl and run direct parse locally. If curl output parses but SDK output fails, bug is in SDK.
- H4 (encoding): run `file -bi resp.raw` and `iconv -f utf-8 -t utf-8 resp.raw > /dev/null` to check validity.

Safe mitigations to reduce customer impact (fast):
- Add defensive JSON cleanup in post-processor with best-effort heuristics (only as temporary):
  - strip trailing commas using regex: `s/,\s*(?=([\]\}]))//g` (apply cautiously).
  - reject if duplicated keys detected (log raw payload).
  - attempt to run `json5` parser as fallback to accept trailing commas, then reserialize to strict JSON for downstream.
- Circuit-breaker: if parser fails, return HTTP 202 "processing" with a retry token and schedule background parse/cleanup (prevents client crash).

Notes on defensive cleanup risks:
- Regex fixes can mask real model logic issues (e.g., model responded with commentary and not intended JSON).
- json5 fallback may accept invalid but semantically wrong outputs. Use with strict logging and alerting.

Triaging timeline (breadcrumbs):
- 2024-10-29 08:42 — first alert: 5% parse errors in 10m window reported by Sentry (route: /v1/generate/chat).
- 2024-10-29 08:50 — rolled back prompt change (pr#842) on staging; errors persisted in prod.
- 2024-10-29 09:12 — staged an instrumentation patch to capture raw tokenized output.
- 2024-10-29 09:47 — found two server traces where chunk boundary happened inside unicode escape (\\uXXXX) — likely streaming reassembly bug.
- 2024-10-29 10:05 — opened INF-1776 (linear) to track investigation.

Notes / heuristics discovered:
- Common model failure modes: trailing commas, extraneous commentary after JSON ("Notes:"), enclosing output in markdown fences (```json), and returning lists when objects expected.
- When the model response contains markdown fences, our streaming layer sometimes emits fence delimiters as separate chunks; post-processor must strip fences before parse.
- Some languages/models emit single quotes — harmless in plain text but invalid JSON. Quick pre-parse replace of top-level single quotes is brittle.

Experiment ideas (next):
- Add a lightweight "output sanitizer" feature flag on the gateway that can be toggled per-route: 1) strip markdown fences, 2) collapse repeated whitespace, 3) attempt json5 parse then strictify. Run for 10% of traffic.
- Add token-level logging for 1% requests to blame model vs transport.
- Create a small fuzz harness that sends many edge-case prompts (asks for JSON with comments, arrays, nested objects) to measure model fidelity across quant/variants.

Immediate next steps (actionable):
- [ ] Push an SDK patch that bypasses streaming reassembly for 2048-byte chunks and compare parse rates (Samir) — due 2024-11-05.
- [ ] Enable gateway flag to capture full response bytes for failing requests (Aisha) — due 2024-10-31.
- [ ] Add SLO alert rule: parser-fail-rate > 0.5% over 15m -> notify #eng-applied-ml and page.
- [ ] Draft customer-facing note for support (says: transient parsing errors; running cleanup and retries) — keep conservative language (Lena).

References / quick links:
- Linear: INF-1776
- PR with recent prompt change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/842
- Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C0123ABC/p1698624000000

Scratch ideas to keep offline (non-prod):
- Train a small LM discriminator that predicts "well-formed JSON" probability given prefix tokens; use as quick gate before returning to SDK.
- Add an optional output schema validator endpoint that can be called in preflight (cheap).

Notes to self (loose):
- When copying example bytes into issue, always sanitize user PII.
- Keep regex-based cleanup as emergency-only; prioritize root-cause.

-- end of playbook scratch --
